name: Aquila
source_summary: A Jewish tentmaker from Pontus, married to Priscilla, who partnered with Paul in ministry and trade, hosted churches in their home, and together with his wife more accurately instructed the eloquent preacher Apollos.
family_friendly_summary: Aquila and his wife Priscilla were tentmakers, the same trade as Paul, and the couple had to leave Rome when the emperor ordered all Jews to leave the city. They settled in Corinth, where Paul met them, worked alongside them, and stayed in their home. Aquila and Priscilla traveled with Paul afterward and became close partners in his ministry, hosting a church that met in their own house in more than one city they lived in. In one memorable story, the couple heard a gifted preacher named Apollos teaching accurately about Jesus but with some incomplete understanding, so they took him aside privately and explained the way of God to him more fully. Aquila and his wife are mentioned together several times in the New Testament as valued partners in Paul's missionary work.
adult_story: Aquila, a Jew originally from Pontus, and his wife Priscilla had recently come from Italy after the emperor Claudius ordered all Jews to leave Rome, and settled in Corinth, where Paul met them and stayed, working together at their shared trade of tentmaking (Acts 18:1-3). The couple accompanied Paul to Ephesus and remained there when he moved on, and it was there that they encountered Apollos, an eloquent and scripturally learned preacher who nonetheless knew "only the baptism of John" -- an incomplete understanding of the gospel; "they took him aside and explained to him the way of God more accurately" (18:18-26), a striking picture of a husband-and-wife team correcting and completing the theology of a gifted public teacher, done privately and without public embarrassment. They hosted a church in their home, first apparently in Ephesus and later again in Rome once they had returned there (Romans 16:3-5; 1 Corinthians 16:19). Paul calls them "my fellow workers in Christ Jesus, who risked their own necks for my life," indicating some unrecorded moment of real danger they faced on his behalf (Romans 16:3-4). Aquila appears consistently alongside his wife across six New Testament references, a couple whose shared trade, shared home, and shared ministry made them some of the most practically valuable partners in Paul's mission (Acts 18:2, 18, 26; Romans 16:3; 1 Corinthians 16:19; 2 Timothy 4:19).
devotionals: Aquila’s story teaches us about ministry partnership; may we look to Jesus, whose grace and truth never fail.
Through Aquila’s experience of teaching, God teaches us to trust His wisdom and follow Jesus faithfully.
